title: Survival phrases (Wichtige Sätze)
summary: The phrases that keep a conversation going when you don't understand, plus please, thank you and sorry.
goals: Ask someone to repeat or to speak slowly
Ask what something is in German
Say please, thank you and sorry

points: Thanks: [[Danke]], [[Danke schön]], and when you're really grateful [[Vielen Dank]] (the v sounds like f). The answer is [[Bitte]] or [[Bitte schön]].
[[Bitte]] also means please. [[Entschuldigen Sie bitte]] is the polite 'excuse me', [[Entschuldigung]] the everyday one. To apologise: [[Entschuldigung]] or [[Es tut mir leid.]] (a long u in tut).
Didn't catch it? [[Wie bitte?]] with a rising voice, or just [[Bitte?]] More explicit: [[Noch einmal, bitte.]] or [[Bitte wiederholen Sie.]]
Languages: [[Sprechen Sie Deutsch?]] - [[Ich spreche kein Englisch.]] or [[Ich spreche etwas Deutsch.]] (a little).
Not knowing: [[Ich weiß nicht.]] (ß sounds like ss) or the casual [[Keine Ahnung.]] (no idea).
Also handy: [[Kein Problem.]], [[Einen Moment, bitte.]], and the three key words [[ja]], [[nein]] and [[vielleicht]] (maybe; v sounds like f).
notes.extra: [[Keine Ahnung]] and [[Kein Problem]] are casual: fine with friends and colleagues.

points: Polite basics: [[Entschuldigung]] (excuse me, sorry; more formal [[Entschuldigen Sie]]), [[danke]], [[danke schön]], [[vielen Dank]], and [[bitte]] (you're welcome, and please).

Every noun has an article, [[der]], [[die]] or [[das]], and a capital letter: [[das Wasser]], [[das Auto]], [[das Haus]], [[das Handy]] (mobile phone), [[das Geld]] (money), [[der Abend]], [[der Hunger]].
Hunger is something you have: [[Ich habe Hunger.]] (I'm hungry).
[[Das ist mein ...]] says what's yours: [[Das ist mein Auto.]] An adjective can stand after [[ist]]: [[Das ist gut.]], [[Das ist schön.]] (that's nice).
Two verbs, [[essen]] (to eat) and [[trinken]] (to drink). Verbs change their ending for each person: [[ich esse]], [[ich trinke]].

sections.title: Your emergency kit
sections.text:
These phrases are worth more than a hundred other words: they let you stay in a conversation even when you understand very little.

Learn them as **whole chunks**. Don't analyse the grammar yet; that comes in Unit 1.

items.note: Point at something while you ask.

items.en: Thank you very much! - You're very welcome!

sections.text: [[Bitte]] works like Russian пожалуйста: please, you're welcome, and 'here you go' when you hand something over, all in one word. Armenian splits it: խնդրում եմ (please) and խնդրեմ (you're welcome, here you go). [[Wie bitte?]] means 'pardon?'.
Say [[Ich verstehe nicht.]] with [[nicht]] at the end. There is no 'do' in German: not 'I do not understand' but literally 'I understand not'.
[[Entschuldigung]] is both 'excuse me' (to get attention, e.g. before asking the way) and 'sorry' (after bumping into someone).

items.question: Someone is speaking too fast. What do you say?
You didn't catch what someone said. What do you say?
items.explanation: Wie bitte? = pardon? Wie geht's? = how are you?
nicht comes at the end: Ich verstehe nicht.
Ich spreche = I speak; ein bisschen = a little.
